_comment: A diagnostic to read, never a score to raise -- the same rule as .cargo/mutants.toml.
`break` is null on purpose. A mutation score that must go up produces tests written to
kill mutants rather than to state invariants, and a test corresponding to no rule breaks
`mutate` lists the six pure modules and nothing else. app.js is 3,200 lines of DOM whose
only coverage is Playwright, which this runner never invokes; mutating it would produce a
wall of survivors saying one thing already known and already ruled on. http.js is the
same. Survivors here mean 'what the node --test suite misses', never 'what is untested'.
The UMD wrapper at the top of each module contributes ~20 unkillable survivors
(typeof module === 'object'). They are noise; read past the first dozen lines of each file.
npm run test:mutants               -- all six, about two minutes
npx stryker run --mutate src/heat.js   -- one file, while writing its tests
